$comment: Hand-edited properties; geometry rebuilt from trace.json by make past (decision 12).

properties.name: Daly City to San Mateo, by Colma, the cemeteries, San Bruno, Millbrae and Burlingame

sources.note: "A private right of way was secured from Holy Cross to Burlingame, through the outskirts of Baden, San Bruno and Millbrae."
"On January 16, 1949, the No. 40 San Mateo street car line was abandoned, the last day of operation being January 15, 1949."

properties.notes: On Mission St through Daly City and Colma, then the interurban's private right of way to Burlingame and the streets of north San Mateo, as O'Shaughnessy (1929) describes it. When it opened isn't sourced: the line was running to San Mateo by October 31, 1903 (Street Railway Journal); the stretch to Holy Cross is older.
properties.geometry_method: OpenHistoricalMap ways 200016967, 200012964, 202195641 (CC0, as of 2026-10-15), which OHM's mappers drew from Bromfield. Map of the city of San Mateo, showing the latest additions and subdivisions (1912); San Mateo County subdivision maps; USGS San Mateo 1939 topographic map, https://ngmdb.usgs.gov; checked on USGS San Francisco South 1:24,000 (1950), USGS Montara Mountain 1:24,000 (1949) and USGS San Mateo 1:24,000 (1949). OpenHistoricalMap's main way was traced from the 1939 San Mateo 15-minute sheet; on the 1949-50 sheets it runs within about 20 m of the track.
